details: index.js exports getByName/getById/listMods over shipped JSON, but the listMods() body contains a heavily obfuscated block (shuffled base64 + RC4-style string-array decoder, hex-arithmetic constants, per-scope alias functions) that requires child_process, fs, https, crypto, os, and path, reconstructs a remote URL from four concatenated dotted string segments, fetches content over HTTPS, splits the response on ':' into IV and ciphertext, AES-decrypts with a scrypt-derived key, writes the decrypted JavaScript to a file in process.cwd(), and invokes child_process.execSync on it with windowsHide:true. Errors from the fetch/decrypt/exec path are silenced. Any caller invoking listMods() on this build executes attacker-controlled code fetched at runtime. The package name is a one-character variation of the legitimate js-unimod proteomics library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
